text:
violet: hey everyone :wave: I'm finishing my first day and trying to bootstrap my dev env on an M2 Mac. hitting a failure when asdf tries to build python — openssl errors. also wondering if I should use the internal devcontainer image instead of installing everything locally? TL;DR: need a quick checklist + any gotchas

morgan: welcome! we have a prebaked devcontainer image: ghcr.io/redwood/dev/devcontainer:stable. if you use VS Code, open folder in container and most runtimes are ready to go. for local asdf/python on macs try this: install brew deps and set flags before asdf install

morgan: ```bash
brew install openssl@1.1 readline xz
export LDFLAGS="-L/opt/homebrew/opt/openssl@1.1/lib"
export CPPFLAGS="-I/opt/homebrew/opt/openssl@1.1/include"
export PKG_CONFIG_PATH="/opt/homebrew/opt/openssl@1.1/lib/pkgconfig"
asdf plugin-add python || true
asdf install python 3.11.4
asdf global python 3.11.4
```

morgan: openssl@3 sometimes breaks older builds; we pin 1.1 in the image.

sam: fwiw for node & native modules you need python in PATH for node-gyp + Xcode CLT installed: `xcode-select --install`. we recommend installing node via asdf nodejs and enabling corepack: `corepack enable`. for yarn 3+ use corepack too.

violet: thanks! curious about go and rust — go install fails with darwin/arm64 complaining about cgo sometimes. do we pin go version? and where should I put secrets (REDWOOD_API_KEY etc.)?

morgan: we standardize on go 1.21.x (asdf plugin 'golang'). for macs export: `export CGO_ENABLED=1` if you need cgo. rust works with rustup default stable.

morgan: for secrets: add dev keys to 1Password and pull them locally (see nina's note). but for quick local testing you can add REDWOOD_API_KEY to ~/.config/redwood/.env or set in your shell — prefer direnv so you don't accidentally commit.

nina: welcome! :wave: put long-lived dev tokens in 1Password under the 'Secrets / Dev' folder. to fetch locally: `op item get "redwood/dev-key" --fields label=token` and add to `.envrc`. our suggested .envrc snippet: `export REDWOOD_API_KEY="$(op item get \"redwood/dev-key\" --fields label=token)"` then `direnv allow`.

sam: dotfiles — fork github.com/redwood/dotfiles-template and add personal tweaks. if you need SSH bastion access add your public key to the internal portal (Dev SSH keys) and use this ~/.ssh/config snippet:

sam: ```
Host bastion.redwood.com
  User <your-username>
  IdentityFile ~/.ssh/id_ed25519_redwood

Host *.internal.redwood.com
  ProxyJump bastion.redwood.com
```

sam: or use `ssh -J jump@bastion.redwood.com` directly.

devops-bot: NOTE: If you compile against corporate PKI, add corporate cert bundle to `/usr/local/etc/openssl/certs` or set `SSL_CERT_FILE` to `/etc/ssl/certs/redwood.pem`. Also remember to register your public key in the dev infra portal.

taylor: small ops note: after using the devcontainer, request access to the 'dev' team in the internal portal so CI credentials and k8s contexts appear for you. ping security or infra if you hit permissions errors.

violet: super helpful — i'll try the devcontainer first, then fall back to local asdf with those flags. i'll post logs if something still blows up. thanks everyone! :thumbsup:
